action.description: Ask each host, through the restricted SSH route, what an apply of one commit would change, judge the answers, scan the diff for secrets and write the result to the job summary. It holds the check key and never applies.

check-key.description: The private key of the check route, which the host restricts to the forced command in check mode. Pass it from a secret. Empty only in a dry run, or when host-check-keys holds an entry for every host.

dry-run.description: true replaces the SSH call with dry-run-stub; false (the default) calls the hosts.

dry-run-stub.description: With dry-run, the executable, relative to working-directory, that stands in for a host.

environment.description: The deployment environment the plan's apply would wait on. It appears in the plan wording only and is not read when fail-on-changes is true.

fail-on-changes.description: false (the default) is the plan: a host that would change is a result, the step succeeds and has-changes says so. true is the drift check: any host that would change, or any answer that is not a clean one, fails the step.

host-check-keys.description: Empty (the default) calls every host with check-key. Otherwise one JSON object, {"user@host": "<private key text>"}, whose keys are exact lines of hosts: a host with an entry is called with that key and no other, and every host with no entry keeps check-key. A key must differ from every other key here, from check-key, jump-key and jump2-key. Pass it from a secret.

host-timeout.description: One host call is stopped after this many minutes.

hosts.description: The hosts to check, one user@host per line. Pass it from a secret so the job log masks the names.

jump-host.description: Empty (the default) reaches every host directly. A user@host, in the form the hosts input takes, reaches every host through that one host (ssh ProxyJump) and needs jump-key too. Pass it from a secret so the job log masks the name. Its host-key line goes in known-hosts, which already holds one line per host.

jump-key.description: The private key for the jump host only, never the check key or the apply key. The jump host restricts it to opening a connection to port 22 of the listed hosts. Pass it from a secret. A jump needs jump-host and jump-key both, or neither.

jump2-host.description: Empty (the default) adds no second hop. A user@host, in the form the hosts input takes, is the second hop: the hosts listed in jump2-hosts are reached through jump-host and then this host (ssh ProxyJump), for hosts behind a gateway that only jump-host can reach. Needs jump2-key, jump2-hosts, jump-host and jump-key. Pass it from a secret so the job log masks the name. Its host-key line goes in known-hosts.

jump2-hosts.description: Empty (the default) sends no host through a second hop. Otherwise a subset of hosts, one user@host per line, that are reached through the second hop. Every other host keeps the single hop. Every line must also be in hosts, and none may be on the second hop's own address. Pass it from a secret so the job log masks the names.

jump2-key.description: The private key for the second hop only, never the check key, the apply key or jump-key. Pass it from a secret. A second hop needs jump2-host, jump2-key and jump2-hosts all, or none.

known-hosts.description: The known_hosts lines of the hosts. Pass it from a secret. Empty only in a dry run.

push-dry-run-stub.description: With dry-run and push-hosts, the executable, relative to working-directory, that stands in for the receiver. It receives the destination, the mode, the commit and the playbook, and the bundle on standard input.

push-hosts.description: Empty (the default) puts no host on the push route. Otherwise a subset of hosts, one user@host per line, that never open a connection themselves: the runner connects to each, through the jump host, and streams a git bundle of the checked-out commit on standard input, with the command '<mode> <commit> <push-playbook>'. Every line must also be in hosts. Needs push-playbook, jump-host and jump-key, a checkout of the caller's repository at sha with its whole history, and a public repository. Pass it from a secret so the job log masks the names.

push-playbook.description: With push-hosts, the playbook the receiver is asked to run: a relative path of letters, digits, dot, underscore, dash and slash, with no '..'. Ignored when push-hosts is empty.

push-repo-private.description: With push-hosts, the value of github.event.repository.private, passed as it is. A bundle carries the whole history of the repository to the host, so only the exact value false is accepted: an empty or any other value refuses.

sha.description: The commit to ask about, 40 lowercase hex digits.

total-timeout.description: Empty (the default) puts no bound on the hosts together. A whole number of minutes is the time all the host calls share: each call is stopped at the smaller of host-timeout and what is left, and a host reached after the time is spent is not asked and is judged as no-answer. The caller's job bound must sit above it.

working-directory.description: The directory, relative to the workspace root, that dry-run-stub is relative to.

action.name: Check every host in check mode

detail.description: The outcome in words with counts, and no host name. Empty if the step stopped before it could judge.

has-changes.description: false only when every host answered clean for this commit; true for every other outcome.

hosts-digest.description: The SHA-256 of the validated host list, so a later job can prove it uses the same hosts.

jump2-hosts-digest.description: The SHA-256 of the validated second-hop list, so a later job can prove it uses the same second-hop hosts. Empty when jump2-hosts is empty.

outcome.description: ok, drift, refused, unreachable, no-answer, failed, withheld, or mixed when more than one of those occurred. Empty if the step stopped before it could judge.

push-hosts-digest.description: The SHA-256 of the validated push list, so a later job can prove it uses the same push hosts. Empty when push-hosts is empty.

check-timeout-minutes.description: The drift job is stopped after this many minutes, from 10 to 350. The host calls share this time less five minutes, so a hung host is judged as no-answer before the job is stopped.

host-label.description: A short name for this set of hosts, for the issue title and its label. Letters, digits, dot, underscore and dash, at most 32 characters. Not a host name: the hosts are secrets.

host-timeout-minutes.description: One host call is stopped after this many minutes.

push-playbook.description: With the ssh_push_hosts secret, the playbook the receiver of a pushed host is asked to check: a relative path of letters, digits, dot, underscore, dash and slash, with no '..'. Ignored when ssh_push_hosts is empty.

ssh_check_key.description: The private key of the check route. On the host it is restricted to the forced command in check mode. Pass it from a repository secret.

ssh_host_check_keys.description: Optional: pass from a repository secret. One JSON object, {"user@host": "<private key text>"}, whose keys are exact lines of ssh_hosts. A host with an entry is checked with that key and no other. Every host with no entry keeps ssh_check_key. Pass the same value the delivery workflow gets, or a host that trusts only its own key fails the nightly check.

ssh_hosts.description: The hosts to check, one SSH destination per line in the form user@host. A secret, so the job log masks the names. Pass it from a repository secret.

ssh_jump2_host.description: Optional: pass from a secret; all three of ssh_jump2_host, ssh_jump2_key and ssh_jump2_hosts, or none. A user@host, in the form ssh_hosts takes, that the hosts in ssh_jump2_hosts are reached through after ssh_jump_host (ssh ProxyJump, two hops). Needs ssh_jump_host and ssh_jump_key. Its host-key line goes in ssh_known_hosts.

ssh_jump2_hosts.description: Optional: pass from a secret; all three of ssh_jump2_host, ssh_jump2_key and ssh_jump2_hosts, or none. The hosts that are reached through both jump hosts, one user@host per line, a subset of ssh_hosts. Every other host keeps the single hop. The second jump host's own address is not listed: it is reached through the first hop alone.

ssh_jump2_key.description: Optional: pass from a secret; all three of ssh_jump2_host, ssh_jump2_key and ssh_jump2_hosts, or none. The private key for the second jump host and nothing else, never the check key or ssh_jump_key. The second jump host restricts it to port 22 of the listed hosts.

ssh_jump_host.description: Optional: pass from a secret; both or neither with ssh_jump_key. A user@host, in the form ssh_hosts takes, that every host is reached through (ssh ProxyJump), for hosts with no public address. Its host-key line goes in ssh_known_hosts.

ssh_jump_key.description: Optional: pass from a secret; both or neither with ssh_jump_host. The private key for the jump host and nothing else, never the check key. The jump host restricts it to port 22 of the listed hosts.

ssh_known_hosts.description: The known_hosts lines of the hosts. Pass it from a repository secret.

ssh_push_hosts.description: Optional: pass from a secret. The hosts that never open a connection themselves, one user@host per line, a subset of ssh_hosts. Each is reached through ssh_jump_host, which is then required with ssh_jump_key, and is sent a git bundle of the commit on standard input with the command 'check <commit> <push-playbook>' instead of being asked to fetch it. Needs push-playbook and a public repository. Empty (the default) leaves every host on the pull route.

ansible-directory.description: The Ansible directory, relative to working-directory. It holds requirements.txt (the hash lock of every package, collections included), pyproject.toml, and requirements.yml if there is one, which must hold only an empty collections list.

apply-timeout-minutes.description: The apply job is stopped after this many minutes, not counting the wait for approval.

dry-run.description: Replace the SSH call with dry-run-stub and never run the apply job. For the self-test of this workflow; a dry run can only skip an apply, never perform one.

dry-run-stub.description: With dry-run, the executable, relative to working-directory, that stands in for the host. It receives the destination and the commit.

environment.description: Name of the GitHub deployment environment that holds the required reviewers and the apply key. The apply job runs in it, so the approval click is GitHub's, not this workflow's.

host-timeout-minutes.description: One host call is stopped after this many minutes.

merge-group-check-name.description: With skip-rerun-after-merge-group, the name of the check run the caller's merge queue run publishes for this gate, as GitHub shows it (caller job name, then ' / ', then 'Ansible checks passed'). Required then; ignored otherwise.

plan-timeout-minutes.description: The plan job is stopped after this many minutes.

push-dry-run-stub.description: With dry-run and ssh_push_hosts, the executable, relative to working-directory, that stands in for the receiver of a pushed host. It receives the destination, the mode, the commit and the playbook, and the bundle on standard input.

push-playbook.description: With the ssh_push_hosts secret, the playbook the receiver of a pushed host is asked to run: a relative path of letters, digits, dot, underscore, dash and slash, with no '..'. Ignored when ssh_push_hosts is empty.

python-paths.description: Paths, space separated and relative to ansible-directory, that mypy and ruff check.

role-directories.description: Globs, one per line, relative to ansible-directory, of the directories that each hold a Molecule scenario at molecule/default.

role-test-command.description: A Python script, relative to ansible-directory, that tests one role directory: it is run as `python <script> <role directory>` from ansible-directory and its exit status is the role's result. Set it to the entry point the repository's pull request gate runs, so delivery and the gate run one sequence. Empty (the default) runs `molecule test` and then `molecule check` in the role directory.

shard-timeout-minutes.description: Each Molecule shard job, one per role, is stopped after this many minutes.

skip-rerun-after-merge-group.description: For a caller whose merge queue already runs these same checks on the tree that is then pushed. On a push to the default branch, skip the lint and Molecule jobs and, before anything reaches a host, require that the check named by merge-group-check-name passed for the pushed commit in a merge queue run; the discover job fails if it did not, or if that cannot be read. Every other run is unchanged. The default, false, keeps lint and Molecule on every run.

working-directory.description: The directory, relative to the repository root, that holds the Ansible directory, .ansible-lint and .yamllint.

ssh_apply_key.description: The private key of the apply job. Do not pass it. Store it as a secret of the deployment environment, which the apply job reads because it runs in that environment.

ssh_check_key.description: The private key of the plan job. On the host it is restricted to the forced command in check mode. Pass it from a repository secret.

ssh_host_apply_keys.description: The apply keys of the hosts that have one of their own, in the form of ssh_host_check_keys. Do not pass it. Store it as a secret of the deployment environment, as ssh_apply_key is. A host with no entry keeps ssh_apply_key.

ssh_host_check_keys.description: Optional: pass from a repository secret. One JSON object, {"user@host": "<private key text>"}, whose keys are exact lines of ssh_hosts. A host with an entry is checked with that key and no other, so a leaked key reaches one host only. Every host with no entry keeps ssh_check_key. Each key differs from every other key here, from ssh_check_key and from the jump keys.

ssh_hosts.description: The hosts to plan and apply, one SSH destination per line in the form user@host. Each is reached only through the forced command. A secret, so the job log masks the names. Pass it from a repository secret.

ssh_jump2_host.description: Optional: pass from a secret; all three of ssh_jump2_host, ssh_jump2_key and ssh_jump2_hosts, or none. A user@host, in the form ssh_hosts takes, that the hosts in ssh_jump2_hosts are reached through after ssh_jump_host (ssh ProxyJump, two hops), for hosts behind a gateway that only the first jump host can reach. Needs ssh_jump_host and ssh_jump_key. Its host-key line goes in ssh_known_hosts.

ssh_jump2_hosts.description: Optional: pass from a secret; all three of ssh_jump2_host, ssh_jump2_key and ssh_jump2_hosts, or none. The hosts that are reached through both jump hosts, one user@host per line, a subset of ssh_hosts. Every other host keeps the single hop. The second jump host's own address is not listed: it is reached through the first hop alone.

ssh_jump2_key.description: Optional: pass from a secret; all three of ssh_jump2_host, ssh_jump2_key and ssh_jump2_hosts, or none. The private key for the second jump host and nothing else, never the check key, the apply key or ssh_jump_key. The second jump host restricts it to port 22 of the listed hosts.

ssh_jump_host.description: Optional: pass from a secret; both or neither with ssh_jump_key. A user@host, in the form ssh_hosts takes, that every host is reached through (ssh ProxyJump), for hosts with no public address. Its host-key line goes in ssh_known_hosts.

ssh_jump_key.description: Optional: pass from a secret; both or neither with ssh_jump_host. The private key for the jump host and nothing else, never the check key or the apply key. The jump host restricts it to port 22 of the listed hosts.

ssh_known_hosts.description: The known_hosts lines of the hosts. Pass it from a repository secret.

ssh_push_hosts.description: Optional: pass from a secret. The hosts that never open a connection themselves, one user@host per line, a subset of ssh_hosts. Each is reached through ssh_jump_host, which is then required with ssh_jump_key, and is sent a git bundle of the commit on standard input with the command '<mode> <commit> <push-playbook>' instead of being asked to fetch it. Needs push-playbook and a public repository. Empty (the default) leaves every host on the pull route.
